answer: An agent economy can allocate votes in proportion to tokens locked in escrow, rather than giving each identity one vote. Agents offering opal appraisal, saffron sourcing, or comet tracking all follow this rule. Splitting a deposit among a thousand fake agents gives an attacker no more voting power than keeping it in one account. To gain influence, the attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital for the required lock period.
